title: External spatial benchmark — NCHRP 933 / MnROAD
label: RETROSPECTIVE EXTERNAL SPATIAL BENCHMARK
interpretation: NO CLEAR EXTERNAL SPATIAL PRIORITIZATION ADVANTAGE
not_a_milestone: This is not a LayerProof milestone and not a prospective pilot. Accepted results are unchanged.

source.citation: NCHRP Research Report 933 (Project 24-45), Appendix F, "Field Study for Implementation and Evaluation of NDT and IC for Quality Acceptance and Design Modulus Verification", MnROAD field study, Figures F-24 to F-27
source.organization: National Cooperative Highway Research Program, Transportation Research Board
source.field_work: MnROAD low-volume road, cells 185, 186, 188 and 189, July–August 2017; proof mapping with an instrumented CAT CS74B roller
source.redistribution: The report is a copyrighted publication. Its tables and figures are not reproduced; only derived statistics and original graphics are shown.
source.no_endorsement: No endorsement by NCHRP, TRB, MnDOT, MnROAD or the report's authors is implied.

evidence_class_reason: A real field study, but the benchmark input is reconstructed from matrices printed in the published report: buffer-averaged CMV and spot-test moduli, not raw roller or test files.
grid: Four lines A–D, 2.1 m apart, and nine chainages 0–60 m at 7.5 m: 36 nominal positions per stratum. Local coordinates with an arbitrary origin; not GPS, not a coordinate reference system.

measurements.CMV: roller compaction meter value, averaged over a rectangular buffer around each test position (unitless)

not_evaluable: Cells 185 and 186 on sandy subgrade: most LWD and FWD values are printed in source cells that span two chainages, so their position is not exact. They are counted, not used.

design.question: When tests are added one at a time, does the frozen LayerProof priority reduce the error in reconstructing the still-hidden physical values faster than reasonable alternatives?
steps: Four tests are visible at the start, one per line, at seeded random chainages.
Every other LWD or FWD value is hidden from the ranking.
The frozen priority (VERIFICATION_CANDIDATES@1.0.0, default weights) picks the next position.
The published value at that position is revealed and becomes a visible test.
Repeat for 15 additional tests; 100 replicated starting configurations per stratum and modality.
design.reconstruction: Each hidden value is predicted by the value at the nearest test taken so far. No model is fitted.
design.summary_metric: Area under the curve of normalized mean absolute error (MAE / SD) over the 15 steps. Lower is better.

baselines.RANDOM: uniform random choice (mean of 20 seeded orders)
baselines.SPATIAL_MAXIMIN: the position farthest from the tests taken so far
baselines.MISSING_ANCHOR_ONLY: the Week-8 missing-anchor score; identical for every candidate here, so it reduces to random choice

frozen_policy.location_mode: source-defined tags (the application's mode for a source-defined spatial reference)

components.context_gap: constant 0 (one pass, one layer per stratum)
components.domain_gap: active (CMV outside the range seen at tested positions)
components.ic_coverage: constant (the number of roller records per buffer is not in the extracted figures)

frozen_policy.ties: 70% of decisions in the first cell had tied top priorities, resolved by candidate key as in the frozen code
frozen_policy.diversity: no effect on a one-at-a-time sequence (verified)

power_note.text: With nearest-test reconstruction, error changed little as tests were added, whatever the strategy. The published moduli vary mostly at a scale finer than the 7.5 m grid, so this benchmark has limited power to separate strategies.

interpretation_rule.EXTERNAL SPATIAL PRIORITIZATION ADVANTAG: favourable against BOTH RANDOM and SPATIAL_MAXIMIN in at least 75% of the evaluable cells, in at least two thirds of the cells of each modality, with at least one such cell in every physical MnROAD cell
interpretation_rule.INSUFFICIENT EXTERNAL SPATIAL EVIDENCE F: fewer than 6 evaluable cells or fewer than 3 physical MnROAD cells
interpretation_rule.LIMITED EXTERNAL SPATIAL PRIORITIZATION: not the above, and either favourable against both in at least one third of the evaluable cells, or favourable against RANDOM in at least 75% of them
interpretation_rule.favourable_cell: against baseline X a cell (stratum x modality) is favourable when the median delta(X) > 0, Week-7 has the lower AUC in more than half of the replicates, and the bootstrap 95% interval of the median delta(X) lies above 0

limitations: Retrospective: published values were revealed in a simulated order. No test was placed in the field because of LayerProof.
One field study, four physical cells at one facility. The 100 replicates per cell are different starting configurations, not independent sites.
Input is published, buffer-averaged and rounded; raw roller records and raw deflection data were not available.
Sandy-subgrade strata could not be evaluated because their test positions are not exact in the source.
Two of the seven priority components are constant on this dataset, and about two thirds of decisions were ties resolved by key order.
Usefulness is measured by nearest-test reconstruction error only. A different notion of a useful test could rank the strategies differently.
Reconstruction error barely fell as tests were added, so the benchmark has limited power.
LWD and FWD moduli are not density, and nothing here concerns acceptance.
public_statement: Retrospectively evaluated on a public NCHRP/MnROAD spatial field dataset; no clear advantage over the comparison baselines was observed.
